metadata.name: Paul's 2nd Missionary Journey
metadata.description: Paul and Silas travel through Asia Minor and into Macedonia and Greece (~49-52 AD)

properties.name: Antioch (Syria)
properties.description: After a sharp disagreement with Barnabas over John Mark, Paul chose Silas and departed, commended by the brothers to the grace of the Lord.

properties.name: Lystra
properties.description: Paul came to Derbe and Lystra, where Timothy, well-spoken of by brothers there, joined them. Paul circumcised him because of the Jews in the area.

properties.name: Troas
properties.description: During the night Paul had a vision of a man from Macedonia pleading, 'Come over to Macedonia and help us.' They concluded God was calling them to preach there.

properties.name: Neapolis
properties.description: Setting sail from Troas, they ran a straight course to Samothrace, and the following day to Neapolis — the port of Philippi in Macedonia.

properties.name: Philippi
properties.event_name: Lydia Believes; Paul and Silas Imprisoned
properties.description: Lydia, a dealer in purple cloth, was converted and baptized. Paul cast out a spirit of divination from a slave girl; Paul and Silas were beaten and jailed. An earthquake freed them; the jailer and his household were baptized.

properties.name: Thessalonica
properties.description: Paul reasoned from Scripture for three Sabbaths that Jesus was the Christ. Some Jews and many God-fearing Greeks believed. A mob attacked Jason's house seeking Paul and Silas.

properties.name: Berea
properties.description: The Bereans received the word with eagerness and examined the Scriptures every day to see if what Paul said was true — called more noble-minded than the Thessalonians.

properties.name: Athens
properties.description: Seeing the city full of idols, Paul preached to the Athenians about the 'unknown god.' Some sneered at the resurrection; others believed, including Dionysius the Areopagite.

properties.name: Corinth
properties.description: Paul stayed 18 months, working with Aquila and Priscilla as tentmakers, and reasoning in the synagogue every Sabbath. Crispus, the synagogue ruler, believed.

properties.name: Ephesus
properties.description: Paul stopped briefly in Ephesus, reasoning in the synagogue. Though they asked him to stay longer, he declined but promised to return if God willed.

properties.name: Caesarea Maritima
properties.description: Paul went up and greeted the church in Jerusalem (likely), then went down to Antioch, completing the second missionary journey.
